transcript: It seems like you didn't get my last transmission So fyi don't don't use tables and don't send me actual like Terminal output if it's really long and complicated just because I'm communicating with you through voice primarily so it It sounded pretty silly hearing all those dashes But I want so help me make sense of this so we have Only a few open code instances that are attached to gossamer Tell me what's wrong with the zombie processes that are attached to gossamer Specifically like where they were at why they're stuck And just run some tests on them and let me know what's going on
output:
I'll investigate the zombie processes attached to gossamer. Let me first look at what's in the workspace and find any running processes.
Let me get more details about the process tree and relationships.
Let me check what the parent processes of these zombies are doing.
Here's what I found about the zombie processes and gossamer:

The six zombie processes you're seeing are NOT actually attached to gossamer. They're orphans from other apps that didn't clean up after themselves. Here's the breakdown:

Two are from zypak-sandbox, which is Bitwarden's sandbox process. They've been zombies for over a day now. Their parent Bitwarden is still alive but never called wait() to reap them. Same situation with the other zypak-sandbox zombie from Equibop.

One is from sober, likely an Electron app, dead for about 23 minutes. Its parent is also a /proc/self/exe process still running but not cleaning up.

Three are from speech-dispatcher, your text-to-speech system. Those are sd_festival, sd_espeak-ng-mb, and sd_openjtalk. They've been dead about 4 minutes. speech-dispatcher is still running but isn't reaping its children.

The real issue with gossamer is different. The wrapper script runs process_one.py every 3 seconds, and process_one.py has a 120-second timeout on opencode. If opencode takes longer than that, it throws a TimeoutExpired error and the wrapper just loops around and tries again. That's why you see multiple opencode instances piling up in terminals. The previous one that timed out is what spawned the current one you're talking to right now.

The four opencode instances in VS Code terminals have been running for hours with high CPU usage, so those are likely stuck or waiting on something. The zombies themselves are harmless but indicate parent processes aren't handling child cleanup properly.
